newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsicans oppose independence from Paris - poll.
newsitem.headline: Corsicans oppose independence from Paris - poll.

text.p: Corsicans overwhelmingly oppose the idea of independence from France and approve Paris' plans to crack down on guerrillas seeking more autonomy for the Mediterranean island, an opinion poll reported on Wednesday.

Ninety-one percent of those polled by telephone for the middle-of-the-road Paris weekly L'Evenement du Jeudi opposed independence for the island, racked by two decades of separatist bombings. Just seven percent were in favour.
Successive governments have ruled out independence for the island, whose 250,000 inhabitants rely heavily on subsidies from the mainland.

Seventy-four percent of Corsicans approved plans by the centre-right government to crack down on the guerrillas after a bomb attack on city hall in Bordeaux, where Prime Minister Alain Juppe is mayor, the IFOP survey found. Only 18 percent disapproved.

But the magazine said the massive opposition to the central question of independence "is not fully satisfactory: it is probable that a large portion of the population favours a process of autonomy within France."

And the survey found that 61 percent of 500 Corsicans polled by telephone on October 12 did not have confidence in Juppe to find lasting solutions for Corsica. Thirty-seven percent expressed confidence in the premier.
Nevertheless, 82 percent said that they did not believe there was a risk of civil war in Corsica.
